subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept an internal yielding glob walker and bootstrap-hook scheduling changes as the bounded fix for bootstrap-context stalls, despite compatibility-sensitive extra-bootstrap matching and prompt/session timing behavior?
rationale: The patch has focused proof and no concrete line-level defect, but replacing the runtime’s glob implementation and changing bootstrap scheduling creates a compatibility contract that automation cannot safely accept on maintainers’ behalf.

options.title: Accept the focused mitigation
options.body: Rebase onto current `main`, require exact-head checks, and accept the bounded glob and scheduling compatibility tradeoff to address the reported bootstrap stall.

options.title: Request one current-head live run
options.body: Ask for a redacted embedded-run or active-channel latency trace on the rebased head before accepting the compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Pause for a different runtime design
options.body: Keep this PR unmerged if maintainers prefer worker isolation or a broader scheduling design over owning a custom glob implementation.

recommendation.title: Accept the focused mitigation
recommendation.body: Rebase onto current `main`, require exact-head checks, and accept the bounded glob and scheduling compatibility tradeoff to address the reported bootstrap stall.

likelyOwner.reason: Their feature history spans the internal hooks, bootstrap path, and guarded workspace reads where the compatibility decision is concentrated.
